translations.title: Rhyme XLVI: She Wounded Me from the Shadows
translations.text:
She wounded me while hiding in the shadows,
sealing her betrayal with a kiss.
She threw her arms around my neck and, from behind,
coldly broke my heart.

And she goes merrily on her way,
happy, smiling, unafraid. Why?
Because no blood flows from the wound...
Because the dead man stands!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XCVI: Far Off Among the Trees
translations.text:
Far off among the trees
of the tangled forest,
do you not see something shining
and weeping? It is a star.

Now it appears closer, shining
as though through gauze
in the doorway of a hermitage.
It is a light.

The end of our swift journey
is here. Disillusion: the light
we followed is neither lamp nor star;
it is an oil lantern.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXXII: I Wandered the World Crying Out
translations.text:
I wandered the world crying out,
“Where is glory?”
And a mysterious voice answered me,
“Farther on... farther on...”

I followed it along the road
the voice pointed out.
At last I found it, but in that instant
it changed into smoke.

Yet the smoke, forming a thick veil,
began to rise,
and, entering the blue expanse,
reached the heavens.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXVIII: I Do Not Know What I Dreamed
translations.text:
I do not know what I dreamed
last night;
it must have been sad, very sad,
for I woke with my anguish still there.

When I sat up, I noticed
my pillow was wet,
and for the first time, seeing it,
my soul filled with bitter pleasure.

A dream that wrings tears from us
is a sad thing;
yet in my sadness I have one joy:
I know I still have tears!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XLI: You Were the Hurricane and I the Tall
translations.text:
You were the hurricane and I the tall
tower defying its might:
you had to break against me or bring me down...
It could not be!

You were the ocean and I the upright
rock waiting steadfast for its surge:
you had to shatter or tear me away...
It could not be!

You were beautiful, I was proud; one used
to sweeping all away, the other to never yielding;
the path was narrow, the clash inevitable...
It could not be!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme VII: In the Dark Corner of the Room
translations.text:
In the dark corner of the room,
perhaps forgotten by its owner,
silent and covered with dust,
stood the harp.

How many notes slept in its strings,
as a bird sleeps among the branches,
waiting for the snow-white hand
that knows how to draw them out!

Alas, I thought, how often genius
sleeps like this deep within the soul,
waiting for a voice, as Lazarus did,
to say, “Rise and walk!”
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XIII: Your Eyes Are Blue, and When You Laugh
translations.text:
Your eyes are blue, and when you laugh
their gentle brightness reminds me
of morning's trembling glow
reflected in the sea.

Your eyes are blue, and when you weep,
the clear tears within them seem to me
like drops of dew
upon a violet.

Your eyes are blue, and when an idea
shines in their depths like a point of light,
it seems to me, in the evening sky,
a wandering star!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LV: Amid the Discordant Din of Revelry
translations.text:
Amid the discordant din of revelry,
an echo of a sigh caressed my ear
like a note of music
from far away.

The echo of a sigh I know,
formed by a breath I have drunk,
the scent of a flower growing unseen
in a shadowy cloister.

My beloved of one day said tenderly,
“What are you thinking of?”
“Nothing...” “Nothing, and you are crying?”
“My sorrow is merry and the wine is sad.”
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XLIII: I Set the Light Aside
translations.text:
I set the light aside and sat
on the edge of the disheveled bed,
silent, gloomy, my fixed gaze
upon the wall.

How long was I like that? I do not know;
when the dreadful intoxication of grief left me,
the lamp was dying, and at my windows
the sun was laughing.

Nor do I know what I thought
in those terrible hours, or what passed through me;
I remember only that I wept and cursed,
and that I grew old that night.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XLVIII: As Iron Is Drawn from a Wound
translations.text:
As iron is drawn from a wound,
I tore her love from my very depths,
though as I did, I felt that with it
I tore away my life.

From the altar I raised to her in my soul,
my will cast down her image,
and the light of faith that burned there
went out before the empty shrine.

Still, to oppose my firm resolve,
her persistent image comes to mind...
When shall I sleep the sleep
that puts an end to dreaming?
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
